item.title: Notes from an edit
item.content:encoded:
• The structure of the article has been altered to have tabs, because I like tabs and they are cool.
  • Alekhine died in March of 1946 under disputed circumstances — there are allegations that he was murdered by the French, or perhaps the Soviets. SCP-928 was recovered by the Foundation in June of 1946. I changed the date from an earlier version.
  • One of Alekhine's rivals was José Raúl Capablanca, the inventor of Capablanca chess. Interestingly enough, I chose Alekhine the first time around for completely unrelated reasons — this is a happy coincidence.

If a human subject comes within three meters of SCP-928, SCP-928 will vanish and reappear adjacent to the subject several seconds later

That sounds familiar.
Eh, I don't get this. It felt a bit jumbled to me, but apparently its a doll that calls out chess moves, which correspond with real world events. Im sure we already have real world event SCPs, but the object here in question feels completely disjointed from its hook. I'm not sure how you rewrote this, Scantron, but I'm going to have to downvote for now.

item.title: This would be better...

For one, do its moves correspond with Foundation personnel only because it's in our possession, or was it created specifically to target foundation activities?

Also, does it controll the corresponding events by moving, or simply move in response to them?
